sentences.text: 3  THIS MISCELLANEOUS FIRST APPEAL FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF THE MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 1.07.2016 PASSED BY MOTOR ACCIDENT CLAIMS TRIBUNAL II, AT BALLARI, IN MVC NO. 209/2015 BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION TO THE APPELLANT.

THESE APPEALS, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY, BASAVARAJA, J., DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT MFA.No.103695/2016 is preferred by the insurance company and MFA.No.100980/2017 is preferred by the claimants,
which arise out of the judgment and award dated 01.07.2016 passed in MVC.N o.209/2015 on the file of the Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal-II, Ballari (hereinafter referred to as the 'Tribunal')..
2. For the sake of convenience, the parties are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal.

3. Brief facts of the case are that on 05.02.2015, U.G.Krishna Murthy was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Regn.No.KA-34/ED-3625 slowly, cautiously and on the proper side of the road and when he was near to the Petrol Bunk at Dudithini-Siddamanahalli road, Kudithini, a NC:
2023:KHC-D:11162-DB lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-02/TB-3447 was parked on the middle of the road without putting any signal lights or indicators and due to which U.G.Krishna Murthy dashed to the said lorry, as a result of which, he sustained grievous injuries.
Immediately, he was shifted to VIMS Hospital, Ballari and later on to Danamma Hospital, Ballari.
The Doctors have conducted operation on his head, but he succumbed to the injuries during treatment.

4. It is contended that the petitioners have incurred a sum of Rs.1,50,000/- towards medical,
transportation and funeral expenses and it is further stated that the deceased was aged about 25 years, working as a labour and earning Rs.450/- per day and used to contribute all his earnings for the maintenance of his family.

The petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter and petitioner Nos.3 and 4 are the parents of the deceased U.G.Krishna Murthy who have filed the instant claim petition seeking compensation.

It is contended that respondent No.1 being the driver, respondent No.2 being the owner and respondent No.3 being the insurer of the offending lorry are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation to the claimants and on all these grounds sought for allowing the claim petition.
6. Respondent Nos.1 to 3 having served with the notices, appeared before the Court and filed the written statements.

Respondent Nos.1 and 2 filed their written statement denying all the averments made in the petition and have contended that the petition filed by the petitioners is false and is not maintainable and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

sentences.text: Respondent No.3-insurance company has also filed its written statement denying the allegations made by the petitioners in the petition.
Respondent No.3 admits that it has issued insurance policy pertaining to the lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-02/TB-3447 subject to various terms and conditions.
It is stated that respondent No.1- driver of NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB
the offending lorry was not holding a valid and effective driving licence to drive the same.
It is also denied that the lorry was parked on the middle of the road without parking lights or signals.
On all these grounds, sought for dismissal of the claim petition.

8. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues, which read as under:
"1. Whether the petitioner proves that on 05.02.2015 at about 8.00 p.m., when the deceased- Krishnamurthy was proceeding on his motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-34/ED-3625 near Petro Bunk, Kuduthini Siddmanahalli road, Kuduthini,
Ballari District, at that time, the respondent No.1-being the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-02/TB-3447 and drove the same in a great speed and in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly stopped the said vehicle on the middle of the road without putting any signals/indicators and due to it, the deceased dashed to the said stationed lorry and sustained injuries all over the body and later succumbed to this injuries?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to the compensation as prayed by them from the respondents?
NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB 3. What order or award?"
9. To prove the case of the petitioners, petitioner No.1 got examined as PW1, and one Ananda, the eyewitness to the incident, got examined as PW2 and 15 documents were got marked at Exs.P1 to P15.
On closure of the petitioners' side evidence, respondent No.3 examined its Administrative Officer as RW1 and got marked 2 documents at Exs.R1 and R2 in support of its defence.

10. On hearing the arguments of both the parties and perusing the material on record, the Tribunal has given its findings to the above issues as following:
"Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative. Issue No.2 : Partly in the Affirmative. Issue No.3 : As per the final Order."
11.

In view of the above findings, the Tribunal has allowed the claim petition in part and awarded the compensation of Rs.13,36,635/- with interest at 6% per NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB annum from the date of the petition till the date of deposit of the award amount holding respondent Nos.1 to 3 jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.

sentences.text: Being aggrieved by the impugned judgment and award passed by the Tribunal, the insurance company has preferred MFA.No.103695/2016 questioning the liability fastened on it and the petitioner Nos.1 to 4/claimants have preferred MFA.No.100980/2017 for enhancement of compensation.
13. Heard learned counsel for the insurance company and the learned counsel for the claimants.
SUBMISSION ON BEHALF OF THE INSURANCE COMPANY:
14. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the insurance company submits that the Tribunal has erred in passing the impugned judgment and award fastening the liability on the insurance company.

The Tribunal ought to have fixed the entire negligence on the part of the deceased rider of the motorcycle on the ground that PW2 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB who is the complainant admitted in his evidence that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle by the deceased.
The deceased without noticing the railway gate which was closed and the vehicles had stopped near the gate, drove the said motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and hit to the lorry from behind.
He also submits that the Tribunal has erred in awarding the compensation toward future prospects and on all these grounds, sought for dismissing the claim petition filed by the petitioner.

SUBMISSION ON BEHALF OF THE CLAIMANTS:
15.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the claimants submits that the Tribunal has rightly held as to the fastening of liability on the insurance company.
He also submits that the Tribunal has not awarded just and proper compensation in accordance with law, facts and as per the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court.
On all these grounds, sought for enhancement of compensation.

On hearing the arguments on both side and on perusal of the material on record, the following points would arise for our consideration:
(1) Whether the insurance company has made out any grounds to interfere as to the liability fastened on it as well as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal?
(2) Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
(3) What order or award?
17.

Our findings to the above points are as under:

sentences.text: We have examined the material placed on record.

On the basis of the complaint filed by one Ananda, Kuduthini Police have registered the case in Crime - 12 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB No.13/2015 against the driver of the lorry bearing Regn.No.AP-02/TB-3447 for the offence punishable under Sections 283 and 337 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860 and Section 187 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and submitted the FIR to the Court.

Thereafter, the Police have visited the spot, conducted spot panchanama and inquest panchanama in the presence of panchas, obtained MV Report, PM Report and recorded the statement of witnesses and also further statement of complainant and on thorough investigation, the Investigating Officer (IO) has submitted the charge sheet against the driver of the offending lorry for the commission of offence punishable under Sections 283 and 304A of the IPC and Section 187 of the M.V.Act.
Apart from this oral evidence, petitioner No.1 also adduced her evidence reiterating the averments made in the petition.
19. During the cross-examination of PW1, the respondents have not questioned as to the charge sheet submitted by IO.

PW2-Anand has also deposed in his - 13 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB evidence as to the accident and during his cross- examination also, the respondents have not questioned as to the FIR and charge sheet.

20. RW1-the Administrative Officer of the insurance company has not whispered anything as to the charge sheet submitted by the IO, but he has stated that the accident has occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the deceased U.G.Krishna Murthy.
Per contra, he has also clearly admitted as to the charge sheet submitted by the IO against the driver of the offending lorry.
The defence set up by the insurance company has not been substantiated by any legal evidence.

Considering the oral and documentary evidence placed by both the parties, the Tribunal has properly appreciated the evidence on record and accordingly given its finding to the effect that the accident occurred due to the negligent act on the part of the driver of the offending lorry.
We do not find any illegality or infirmity as to the findings given by the - 14 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB Tribunal in this regard.
Hence, we answer the Point No.1 in the negative.

sentences.text: With regard to the quantum of compensation is concerned, para Nos.22 to 29 of the judgment,

the Tribunal has observed as under:
"22. Loss of dependency:-
It is stated by the petitioners that the deceased was working as a labour and was earning Rs.450/- per day but the petitioners have not produced any documents to show the same.
So, under such circumstances, the notional income of the deceased is taken at Rs.6,000/-p.m.
The age of the deceased as stated by the petitioners in their petition is 25 years and the same has been mentioned in the post-mortem report which is produced by the petitioners at Ex.P.9.

So if the said age is taken in to consideration then the proper multiplier that is applicable as per Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009 ACJ 1298, will be 18 and when the notional income of the deceased is taken at Rs.6,000/- p.m. then the annual income of the deceased will be Rs.72,000/-.

entities.text: Sarla Verma and others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation and another reported in 2009 ACJ 1298
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
So, the said amount will come to Rs.9,60,000/- (Rs.72,000/- X 18 =
Rs.12,96,000/-).
Since the deceased has left his wife, son and parents, so, 1/4th is deducted - 15 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB towards the personal needs and maintenance of the deceased.

So, after deduction of 1/4th, the amount of dependency will come to Rs.9,72,000/- (Rs.12,96,000/- -
Rs.3,24,000/- = Rs.9,72,000/-).
23. Loss of expectancy:-
Since the deceased has left behind his wife, son and parents, so, I hold that the petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
24. Loss of consortium:- Under the head loss of consortium for the bereaved spouse, I hold that the petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.
25. Funeral expenses:-Under the head loss of funeral expenses, I hold that the petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.30,000/- under this head.

26. Loss of love and affection:- Under the head loss of love and affection, I hold that the petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.30,000/-.
27.
Medical expenses:-

The petitioners have stated in their petition that immediately after the - 16 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB accident, the deceased was shifted to VIMS Hospital, Ballari and later on he was shifted to Danamma Hospital, Ballari as an inpatient and the doctors conducted operation on the head and while taking treatment in the said Hospital U.G.Krishna Murthy succumbed to the injuries and the petitioners have produced 27 medical bills to show the same at Ex.P.13 amounting to Rs.44,633/-, which is rounded off to Rs.44,635/-.
so, I hold that the petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.44,635/- under this head.

sentences.text: Loss of future prospects:- Since the deceased was stated to be a labour and was aged about 25 years and the burden of maintaining the family was upon him.

So I am of the opinion that towards loss of future prospects the petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.2,00,000/-.
29.

So, in all, I hold that the petitioners are entitled to compensation of Rs.13,36,635/- +
(Rs.9,72,000/- + Rs.30,000/- + Rs.30,000/- + Rs.30,000/- + Rs.30,000/- + Rs.2,00,000/- =
Rs.13,36,635/-)."
22.

The Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.6,000/- per month which is not - 17 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB inconsonance with the chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority.

The Tribunal has also not awarded the compensation as per the judgment of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the cases of SARLA VERMA AND OTHERS Vs. DELHI TRANSPORT CORPORATION AND ANOTHER1; NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS2; and MAGMA GENERAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs. NANU RAM ALIAS CHUHRU RAM AND OTHERS3.

As the accident is of the year 2015, in view of the chart issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the notional of the deceased is assessed at Rs.8,000/-.
24.
Considering the age of the petitioner, in view of the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Sarla Verma (supra), the appropriate multiplier would be '18'.
In view of the decision in the case of PRANAY SETHI (supra) the future prospects at 40% is to be added to the income of the deceased which comes to Rs.11,200/- (i.e., Rs.8,000/- + 40%).
As the number of dependents are four, 1/4th of the income is to be deducted towards the personal expenses, which comes to Rs.8,400/- (Rs.11,200/- less 1/4th).

Thus, the claimants are entitled for compensation towards loss of dependency at Rs.18,14,400/- (i.e., Rs.8,400/- X 12 [months] X 18 [multiplier]).
26.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and also keeping in mind the above said decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court, it is just and proper to award the compensation to the petitioners-claimants as under:

ORDER
(i) MFA.No.100980/2017 preferred by the appellants/claimants is hereby partly allowed.
(ii) MFA.No.103695/2016 preferred by the insurance company is hereby dismissed.

(iii) The impugned judgment and award dated 01.07.2016 passed in MVC.No.209/2015 on the file of the learned Motor Accidents Claim Tribunal-II,
Ballari is modified.

It is held that the respondent Nos.1 to 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the total compensation amount of Rs.20,04,400/- to the petitioners- claimants with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization as against Rs.13,36,635/- awarded by the Tribunal.

8. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Tribunal framed the following issues, which read as under:

Ballari District, at that time, the respondent No.1-being the driver of the Lorry bearing Reg.No.AP-02/TB-3447 and drove the same in a great speed and in a rash and negligent manner and suddenly stopped the said vehicle on the middle of the road without putting any signals/indicators and due to it, the deceased dashed to the said stationed lorry and sustained injuries all over the body and later succumbed to this injuries?
2.
Whether the petitioners are entitled to the compensation as prayed by them from the respondents?
On hearing the arguments on both side and on perusal of the material on record, the following points would arise for our consideration:
(1) Whether the insurance company has made out any grounds to interfere as to the liability fastened on it as well as the quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal?
(2) Whether the claimants are entitled for enhancement of compensation?
(3) What order or award?

opennyai_summary.arguments:
14. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the insurance company submits that the Tribunal has erred in passing the impugned judgment and award fastening the liability on the insurance company.
The Tribunal ought to have fixed the entire negligence on the part of the deceased rider of the motorcycle on the ground that PW2 - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC-D:11162-DB who is the complainant admitted in his evidence that the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the motorcycle by the deceased.
The deceased without noticing the railway gate which was closed and the vehicles had stopped near the gate, drove the said motorcycle in rash and negligent manner and hit to the lorry from behind.
Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the claimants submits that the Tribunal has rightly held as to the fastening of liability on the insurance company.
He also submits that the Tribunal has not awarded just and proper compensation in accordance with law, facts and as per the decisions of the Hon'ble Apex Court.
On all these grounds, sought for enhancement of compensation.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
